paleo-indians.name: Paleo-Indians
paleo-indians.summary: The first peoples to inhabit the Americas toward the end of the last Ice Age, likely arriving from Asia in several waves, known mainly through stone tools such as projectile points.

megafauna.name: Megafauna
megafauna.summary: Large animals, generally over about 45 kilograms; most large mammal species went extinct in the late Pleistocene from around 50,000 years ago, possibly due to humans or climate change.

midden.name: Midden
midden.summary: An old dump of domestic waste, often including shells and bones, that lets archaeologists study the diets and daily habits of past societies.

mesa-verde-national-park.name: Mesa Verde
mesa-verde-national-park.summary: A US national park in Colorado preserving thousands of Ancestral Puebloan sites, including the Cliff Palace, and seasonally inhabited by Paleo-Indians from around 7500 BCE.

spear-thrower.name: Atlatl (spear-thrower)
spear-thrower.summary: A hand-held tool using leverage to launch a dart or spear at greater speed, with a cup or spur at the end that holds the spear's butt during the throw.

watson-brake.name: Watson Brake
watson-brake.summary: An archaeological site in Louisiana dated to about 3500 BCE, the oldest known earthwork mound complex in North America, built over centuries by hunter-gatherers rather than a settled farming society.

cooper-bison-kill-site.name: Cooper Bison Kill Site
cooper-bison-kill-site.summary: Archaeological site in Oklahoma from around 10,800-10,200 BCE, where hunters killed bison; it yielded the Cooper Bison Skull, painted with a red zigzag and the oldest known painted object in North America.

vero-man.name: Vero man
vero-man.summary: Fossilized human bones found near Vero, Florida in 1915–1916 alongside remains of Ice Age animals, now confirmed to date to the Pleistocene.

lindenmeier-site.name: Lindenmeier site
lindenmeier-site.summary: An archaeological site in northeastern Colorado with the most extensive known Folsom culture campsite, dated to about 10,300 BCE, and a National Historic Landmark since 1961.

russell-cave-national-monument.name: Russell Cave
russell-cave-national-monument.summary: A U.S. national monument in Alabama with a large cave entrance used as a seasonal shelter by prehistoric peoples from around 6500 BCE to 1650 CE.

kennewick-man.name: Kennewick Man
kennewick-man.summary: A Native American man who lived about 8,400 to 8,700 years ago, whose remains were found in 1996 near Kennewick, Washington, sparking a long legal and scientific dispute.

old-cordilleran-culture.name: Old Cordilleran culture
old-cordilleran-culture.summary: An ancient Native American culture of the Pacific Northwest, from about 8000–9000 BC to 3500 BC, known for simple leaf-shaped stone spear points and a focus on hunting large mammals.

folsom-tradition.name: Folsom tradition
folsom-tradition.summary: A Paleo-Indian culture across central North America from about 10,800 to 10,200 BCE, identified by distinctive projectile points found with extinct bison bones.

cascade-point.name: Cascade point
cascade-point.summary: A leaf-shaped stone projectile point linked to the Cascade culture of the Pacific Northwest, used from about 9000-10000 BCE to roughly 5500 BCE.

clovis-point.name: Clovis point
clovis-point.summary: A fluted stone spearpoint made by the prehistoric Clovis culture, found widely across North America and dated to roughly 13,400 to 12,700 years ago.

clovis-culture.name: Clovis culture
clovis-culture.summary: Paleoindian archaeological culture in North America (about 13,050–12,750 years ago), known for distinctive fluted stone points and hunting mammoths and other megafauna.

koster-site.name: Koster Site
koster-site.summary: Prehistoric site in Illinois occupied from about 7500 BCE to 1000 CE; among its finds are dog burials dated to 9,900 years ago, among the oldest dog remains found in the Americas.

swan-point-archaeological-site.name: Swan Point Archaeological Site
swan-point-archaeological-site.summary: An Alaskan archaeological site discovered in 1991, dated to about 14,000 years ago and holding the oldest undisputed evidence of human habitation in the Americas.

zhokhov-island.name: Zhokhov Island
zhokhov-island.summary: An island in the East Siberian Sea, part of Russia's Yakutia region, northeast of the New Siberian Islands.

dennis-stanford.name: Dennis Stanford
dennis-stanford.summary: An American archaeologist (1943-2019) who, with Bruce Bradley, proposed the Solutrean hypothesis linking prehistoric Iberian stone tool technology to the later Clovis culture in the Americas.

warner-valley.name: Warner Valley
warner-valley.summary: A remote valley in south-central Oregon with a chain of lakes and wetlands, inhabited by Native Americans for thousands of years before 19th-century European explorers arrived.

ouachita-river.name: Ouachita River
ouachita-river.summary: A 605-mile river running through Arkansas and Louisiana that joins the Tensas River to form the Black River; the 25th-longest river in the United States.

horr-s-island.name: Horr's Island
horr-s-island.summary: An Archaic-period archaeological site on an island in Southwest Florida with four mounds and a shell ring, including one of the oldest known mound burials in the eastern United States, dated to about 3400 years ago.

mound-builders.name: Mound Builders
mound-builders.summary: General term for various pre-Columbian North American cultures that built earthwork mounds over more than 5,000 years, an early sign of complex society.

archaic-period-north-america.name: Archaic period (North America)
archaic-period-north-america.summary: A North American cultural stage lasting from about 8000 to 1000 BC, defined by subsistence economies based on nuts, seeds and shellfish before the adoption of farming.

beringia.name: Beringia
beringia.summary: A prehistoric region linking Siberia and Alaska, including a land bridge that let a small human population cross from Asia before spreading into the Americas.

last-glacial-maximum.name: Last Glacial Maximum
last-glacial-maximum.summary: The period between about 26,000 and 20,000 years ago when ice sheets reached their greatest extent, lowering sea levels and expanding deserts worldwide.

peyote.name: Peyote
peyote.summary: A small, spineless cactus containing the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline, used for over 5,000 years by Indigenous peoples of the Americas in ceremonies and folk medicine.

mescaline.name: Mescaline
mescaline.summary: A naturally occurring psychedelic drug found in cacti such as peyote, used recreationally, spiritually and medically, producing altered perception lasting several hours.

alaskan-malamute.name: Alaskan Malamute
alaskan-malamute.summary: Large spitz-type dog breed originally bred to haul heavy freight as a sled dog, related to other Arctic breeds such as the Siberian Husky and Samoyed.

peruvian-hairless-dog.name: Peruvian Hairless Dog
peruvian-hairless-dog.summary: A hairless dog breed native to Peru and the only indigenous dog breed still living in South America, long associated with Andean civilizations.

ancient-beringian.name: Ancient Beringians
ancient-beringian.summary: A human genetic lineage known from an infant's genome at Alaska's Upward Sun River site, dated to about 11,500 years ago, which diverged from the ancestors of Native Americans around 20,000 years ago.

laurentide-ice-sheet.name: Laurentide ice sheet
laurentide-ice-sheet.summary: A massive ice sheet that covered most of Canada and the northern United States at various times over the past 2.58 million years, carving out the Great Lakes.

cordilleran-ice-sheet.name: Cordilleran ice sheet
cordilleran-ice-sheet.summary: A major ice sheet that repeatedly covered large parts of North America during glacial periods over roughly the last 2.6 million years.

old-copper-complex.name: Old Copper complex
old-copper-complex.summary: An archaeological culture of North America's Great Lakes region, known for widespread copper tools, weapons and ornaments dated from about 6500 to 1580 BCE.
